text: # Operating Systems An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services that allow application programs to run. It acts as an interface between software and physical hardware. ## Processes A process is a program in execution. The operating system creates and manages processes, allocates resources, and schedules them for execution. Processes may contain multiple threads. Threads share certain process resources while allowing multiple activities to execute concurrently.

Context switching allows the CPU to move between runnable tasks. ## CPU Scheduling CPU scheduling determines which ready process should execute. Common scheduling approaches include first-come first-served, shortest-job-first, priority scheduling, and round-robin. Scheduling goals can include reducing waiting time, improving response time, and keeping the processor efficiently utilized. ## Memory Management Operating systems manage physical memory and provide processes with address spaces.

Virtual memory allows systems to use secondary storage as an extension of physical memory. Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages and frames. A page table maps virtual pages to physical frames. If a required page is not currently in memory, a page fault can occur. ## File Systems File systems organize persistent information on storage devices. They provide operations for creating, reading, writing, and deleting files and directories.

File allocation methods determine how blocks are assigned to files. File systems also maintain metadata such as file size, ownership, permissions, and timestamps. ## Devices and Security Operating systems interact with hardware through device drivers and I/O mechanisms. Buffering and caching can improve performance when devices are slower than the CPU. Security mechanisms include user accounts, permissions, isolation, authentication, and access control.

These controls help prevent one process or user from accessing resources without permission. Operating systems therefore coordinate processes, memory, storage, devices, and security so that applications can run reliably.
